verdict.rationale: Every must-have requirement is unmatched: the capability profile is built entirely from n8n-based inventory/invoicing automation evidence, with no artifact touching HL7v2, FHIR, HIPAA, clinical data, or pipeline consolidation. The most consequential and buildable gaps are technical — direct HL7v2/FHIR segment-mapping experience (req-2) and the twelve-path consolidation scope (req-9) — both explicitly probed in the technical interview and completely unevidenced. Closing even a narrow version of these with a demonstrable artifact would materially change how the candidate can answer the interview's core technical questions. This does not resolve the non-technical gaps (HIPAA operating experience, on-call track record, SME-translation disposition, implied seniority), which remain real and unaddressed by any build; the operator should treat this posting as a stretch even after building.
verdict.criteria_applied: Must-have requirements were weighed first; a gap was treated as decisive only if it was both must-have and of kind technical, since only technical gaps are closable by an artifact. Domain_experience, track_record and disposition gaps (HIPAA experience, on-call history, SME translation, seniority) were recorded as real but non-decisive because no build closes them — they would remain open even after a strong technical artifact.

alternatives.rejection_reason: The two must-have technical requirements most likely to be tested directly in the 90-minute technical interview (HL7v2/FHIR segment mapping, multi-format pipeline consolidation) have no supporting evidence anywhere in the profile, so applying without addressing them risks a technical interview failure that a short build could partially mitigate.
